neighbours.label: hot weather: heat / hot / scorching / high temperatures of the day or season
fire: We set off at dawn so we could reach the summit before the midday heat.
By early afternoon the parking lot was baking in the summer sun and it was too hot to stand.
The farmers rest in the shade during the hottest hours of the day.
Officials warned that the heat wave would push temperatures past 105 degrees.
Our tent became unbearably hot as soon as the sun rose over the dunes.
Marathon runners struggled in the scorching conditions on Sunday.
Dogs should not be left in cars on hot July afternoons.
The heat in the desert canyon was so intense that our water ran out by noon.
quiet: We set off at dawn so we could reach the summit before the afternoon storms.
By early afternoon the parking lot was flooded after the rain and it was too wet to stand.
The farmers rest in the shade during the longest hours of the harvest.
Officials warned that the storm would push the river past its banks.
Our tent became unbearably damp as soon as the fog rolled over the dunes.
Marathon runners struggled in the windy conditions on Sunday.
Dogs should not be left in cars on busy shopping afternoons.
The wind in the desert canyon was so strong that our tent blew away by noon.
